\label{app:t20_prediction_timeline}

Two versions of the $T{=}20$ prediction file exist, reflecting an evolving statistical protocol:

\paragraph{V1 (git-committed, \texttt{bad72cc}).} Predictions derived from $T{=}10$ PermG results using \emph{raw} $p$-values. At $\alpha{=}0.60$, v1 counted 3/8 pairs with raw $p{<}0.05$, predicting 3/8 detections at $T{=}20$. The observed result (0/8 FDR-significant) does not match.

The fifth prediction ($\alpha{=}0.45$: predicted 0/8 under ceiling model, observed 5/8) falsified the ceiling hypothesis in favor of the power-limited interpretation (\S\ref{sec:theory}).

\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

\paragraph{Methodological pitfalls.}
\label{sec:pitfalls}
Lead-lag analysis in iterative model collapse is fragile along three axes, each documented with data from \S\ref{sec:regime}--\ref{sec:dose_response}.
\emph{Method sensitivity}: five detection methods applied to identical data yield forward significance rates spanning 0\% to 92\%, with inter-method agreement at $\kappa{=}0.185$.
\emph{Spurious regression}: first-differencing eliminates canary$\to$perplexity associations ($F{\approx}0$, $p{=}0.99$) while preserving canary$\to$diversity (24/24$\to$24/24), exposing an entire analysis channel as trend-driven~\cite{granger1974spurious}.
\emph{Regime dependence}: the same Granger test shifts from 0/8 to 6/8 significant pairs across a 5-percentage-point boundary.

\subsection{Method Sensitivity Analysis}
\label{sec:mmct}
We compare five lead-lag detection methods---naive cross-correlation, differenced cross-correlation, threshold onset, permutation Granger causality (PermG), and Toda--Yamamoto~\cite{toda1995statistical}---in a multi-method comparison~\cite{simonsohn2020specification} calibrated against null-control ($\alpha{=}0.0$) data where any detection is a false positive.
Detection results use equal-weight majority voting ($K{\geq}3$ of 5 methods, each contributing one vote per pair) with forward-direction filtering; FPR-inverse weighting is used only in exploratory method ranking (Appendix~\ref{app:weight_robustness}).
Each method embodies different assumptions: naive cross-correlation is assumption-free but produces 92\% null-control FPR; differenced cross-correlation controls for trends but lacks directional separation; threshold onset is power-limited at $T{=}11$; Toda--Yamamoto avoids pre-testing for unit roots; PermG uses a nonparametric permutation null with built-in directionality.
Pooled null-control FPR across three seeds (cluster-bootstrap 95\% CI): PermG 0\% $[0, 0]$, Toda--Yamamoto 17\% $[0, 25]$, DiffXCorr 38\% $[25, 50]$, NaiveXCorr 92\% $[88, 100]$ (Appendix~\ref{app:fpr_independence}).
DiffXCorr's empirical FPR (38\%) substantially exceeds its simulated rate (4.2\% under AR(1) DGP), indicating that model-collapse nonstationarity extends beyond simple autoregressive structure.
Under all four weighting schemes (equal, FPR-inverse, capped, rank-based), PermG is the only method maintaining zero null-control FPR alongside consistent detection at $\alpha \geq 0.50$.
This finding---that method choice alone can shift conclusions from universal significance to complete null on identical data---motivates reporting method sensitivity as a primary result rather than relegating it to a robustness check.

\paragraph{Permutation Granger causality.}
PermG tests whether past values of canary metric $X$ improve prediction of downstream metric $Y$ beyond $Y$'s own history; Granger precedence establishes temporal predictive improvement, not true causality~\cite{shojaie2022granger}.
We apply 5{,}000 permutations~\citep{phipson2010permutation} on first-differenced series with Benjamini--Hochberg FDR correction at $q{=}0.05$ across 8 validated canary$\to$downstream pairs (2 canaries $\times$ 4 downstream metrics).
The permutation test controls Type~I error exactly by construction (exchangeable null distribution); BH-FDR correction remains valid under positive regression dependence~\cite{benjamini2001control}, and our 0/24 null-control rejections across three seeds validate this theoretical guarantee (within-seed ICC${=}0.34$, cluster-adjusted 95\% CI $[0\%, 41\%]$; Appendix~\ref{app:fpr_independence}).
Simulation under non-stationary AR(1) DGP ($\varphi{=}0.95$--$0.99$) reveals PermG FPR inflation to ${\sim}10\%$; however, our empirical series exhibit low stochastic persistence (null token entropy $\varphi{=}-0.51$; first-differenced distinct-1 $\varphi{<}0.44$), and 0/24 null rejections confirm adequate size control (Appendix~\ref{app:nonstationarity}).
The same simulation shows PermG retains ${\sim}80\%$ of raw-levels power at $T{=}11$ versus ${\sim}61\%$ for standard first-differencing, justifying the permutation approach at short series lengths.

\subsection{Power Scaling Interpretation}
\label{sec:theory}

We apply the standard Wald test power scaling framework to PermG, decomposing the non-centrality parameter into signal and resolution components.
Detection power scales as $\mathrm{Power}(\alpha, T) = \Phi\bigl(S(\alpha) \cdot R(\alpha) \cdot \sqrt{T} / \sigma\bigr)$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF, $\sigma$ is the residual standard deviation from the VAR(1) model under the permutation null, and $\sqrt{T}$ is a conservative lower bound from standard power analysis.
This has the form of a standard $z$-test power function $\Phi(\delta\sqrt{T}/\sigma)$; the domain-specific decomposition of $\delta$ into signal $S(\alpha)$ (magnitude of distributional shift, monotonically increasing) and resolution $R(\alpha)$ (generational gap between canary and downstream responses) explains the non-monotonic dose-response:
$R(\alpha)$ drops at $\alpha{\approx}0.60$ when relaxation time matching compresses both responses into a single generation, producing a local minimum in $S \times R$ despite rising $S$.
This predicts four regimes: \emph{blind} ($S$ below detection floor), \emph{onset} ($S$ crosses threshold, $R$ high), \emph{synchronous dip} ($R \to 0$), and \emph{detection} ($S$ dominates).
$T{=}20$ validates the power-limited interpretation: detection counts are T-invariant at $\alpha \geq 0.50$ (6/8$\to$6/8) but increase at $\alpha{=}0.45$ (0/8$\to$5/8), confirming that the blind zone reflects insufficient power rather than absent signal (\S\ref{sec:dose_response}).

1	\section{Cascade Ordering}
2	\label{sec:cascade}
3	
4	We formalize the empirical regularity that entropy is the earliest available canary metric for diversity collapse.
5	Under mode amplification---the assumption that MLE on peaked distributions concentrates probability toward high-frequency tokens~\cite{shumailov2024curse,dohmatob2024tale}---we derive a formal ordering of metric responses with theoretical grounding (proofs in Appendix~\ref{app:cascade_theory}).
6	
7	\begin{proposition}[Entropy leads diversity]\label{thm:entropy_leads}
8	Under mode amplification: \textup{(a)} entropy can decrease while the $\epsilon$-effective support $S_\epsilon(p) {=} |\{i: p_i > \epsilon\}|$ (hence distinct-$n$) is unchanged; \textup{(b)} if distinct-$n$ decreases, entropy has already decreased.
9	\end{proposition}
10	
11	The asymmetry arises because entropy responds to any mass redistribution (first-order), while diversity changes only when a token probability crosses the generation threshold~$\epsilon$; the margin $\gamma = \min_{i: p_i > \epsilon}(p_i - \epsilon)$ quantifies how much shift diversity absorbs silently.
12	
13	\begin{proposition}[Diversity lag $\geq 1$ generation]\label{prop:div_lag}
14	If the per-generation perturbation satisfies $\alpha\|\mathcal{T}(p_t) - p_t\|_\infty < \gamma(p_t, \epsilon)$ through entropy onset $t_H$, then diversity onset $t_D \geq t_H + 1$.
15	\end{proposition}
16	
17	ECE co-moves with entropy at zero lag: peakier conditionals simultaneously decrease per-token entropy and increase confidence ($\Delta\mathrm{ECE} \approx \Delta C > 0$ whenever $\Delta\bar{H} < 0$; qualitative argument, Appendix~\ref{app:cascade_theory}).
18	The predicted cascade $\{H, \mathrm{ECE}\} \to \mathrm{Distinct}$-$n$ is confirmed in 15/15 experiments at $\alpha \geq 0.30$ (within-domain WikiText, $2\sigma$ onset threshold): entropy and ECE onset at generation~1, distinct-$n$ at generation~2 ($t_H{=}t_{\mathrm{ECE}}{=}1$, $t_D{=}2$ uniformly; \S\ref{sec:regime}; Appendix~\ref{app:moment_cascade}).
19	Five low-$\alpha$ experiments show no detectable onset, leaving the ordering undefined below the detection floor.
20	The cascade establishes entropy as the \emph{optimal canary metric}---the earliest available signal---and explains PermG's directional selectivity: forward tests detect temporal precedence (6/8) while reverse tests find none (0/8) at $\alpha \geq 0.50$.

\label{prop:detection-bound}

19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

\section{Method}
\label{sec:method}

\paragraph{Methodological pitfalls.}
\label{sec:pitfalls}
Lead-lag analysis in iterative model collapse is fragile along three axes, each documented with data from \S\ref{sec:regime}--\ref{sec:dose_response}.
\emph{Method sensitivity}: five detection methods applied to identical data yield forward significance rates spanning 0\% to 92\%, with inter-method agreement at $\kappa{=}0.185$.
\emph{Spurious regression}: first-differencing eliminates canary$\to$perplexity associations ($F{\approx}0$, $p{=}0.99$) while preserving canary$\to$diversity (24/24$\to$24/24), exposing an entire analysis channel as trend-driven~\cite{granger1974spurious}.
\emph{Regime dependence}: the same Granger test shifts from 0/8 to 6/8 significant pairs across a 5-percentage-point boundary.

\subsection{Method Sensitivity Analysis}
\label{sec:mmct}
We compare five lead-lag detection methods---naive cross-correlation, differenced cross-correlation, threshold onset, permutation Granger causality (PermG), and Toda--Yamamoto~\cite{toda1995statistical}---in a multi-method comparison~\cite{simonsohn2020specification} calibrated against null-control ($\alpha{=}0.0$) data where any detection is a false positive.
Detection results use equal-weight majority voting ($K{\geq}3$ of 5 methods, each contributing one vote per pair) with forward-direction filtering; FPR-inverse weighting is used only in exploratory method ranking (Appendix~\ref{app:weight_robustness}).

DiffXCorr's empirical FPR (38\%) substantially exceeds its simulated rate (4.2\% under AR(1) DGP), indicating that model-collapse nonstationarity extends beyond simple autoregressive structure.
Under all four weighting schemes (equal, FPR-inverse, capped, rank-based), PermG is the only method maintaining zero null-control FPR alongside consistent detection at $\alpha \geq 0.50$.
This finding---that method choice alone can shift conclusions from universal significance to complete null on identical data---motivates reporting method sensitivity as a primary result rather than relegating it to a robustness check.

\paragraph{Permutation Granger causality.}
PermG tests whether past values of canary metric $X$ improve prediction of downstream metric $Y$ beyond $Y$'s own history; Granger precedence establishes temporal predictive improvement, not true causality~\cite{shojaie2022granger}.
We apply 5{,}000 permutations~\citep{phipson2010permutation} on first-differenced series with Benjamini--Hochberg FDR correction at $q{=}0.05$ across 8 validated canary$\to$downstream pairs (2 canaries $\times$ 4 downstream metrics).

\label{sec:theory}

2	\label{sec:cascade}
3	
4	We formalize the empirical regularity that entropy is the earliest available canary metric for diversity collapse.
5	Under mode amplification---the assumption that MLE on peaked distributions concentrates probability toward high-frequency tokens~\cite{shumailov2024curse,dohmatob2024tale}---we derive a formal ordering of metric responses with theoretical grounding (proofs in Appendix~\ref{app:cascade_theory}).

7	\begin{proposition}[Entropy leads diversity]\label{thm:entropy_leads}
8	Under mode amplification: \textup{(a)} entropy can decrease while the $\epsilon$-effective support $S_\epsilon(p) {=} |\{i: p_i > \epsilon\}|$ (hence distinct-$n$) is unchanged; \textup{(b)} if distinct-$n$ decreases, entropy has already decreased.
9	\end{proposition}
10	
11	The asymmetry arises because entropy responds to any mass redistribution (first-order), while diversity changes only when a token probability crosses the generation threshold~$\epsilon$; the margin $\gamma = \min_{i: p_i > \epsilon}(p_i - \epsilon)$ quantifies how much shift diversity absorbs silently.
12	
13	\begin{proposition}[Diversity lag $\geq 1$ generation]\label{prop:div_lag}
14	If the per-generation perturbation satisfies $\alpha\|\mathcal{T}(p_t) - p_t\|_\infty < \gamma(p_t, \epsilon)$ through entropy onset $t_H$, then diversity onset $t_D \geq t_H + 1$.
15	\end{proposition}
16	
17	ECE co-moves with entropy at zero lag: peakier conditionals simultaneously decrease per-token entropy and increase confidence ($\Delta\mathrm{ECE} \approx \Delta C > 0$ whenever $\Delta\bar{H} < 0$; qualitative argument, Appendix~\ref{app:cascade_theory}).

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

When language models train iteratively on their own output, the training distribution progressively loses its tail modes, a phenomenon termed model collapse~\cite{shumailov2024curse,alemohammad2024mad}.
Lexical diversity narrows, calibration deteriorates, and each generation inherits the systematic biases of its predecessors.
As machine-generated text becomes prevalent on the web, such feedback loops pose a growing risk to production training pipelines.
By the time standard quality metrics register degradation, the underlying distribution may have already shifted irreversibly.

This threat motivates a fundamental question: \emph{what does the detectability landscape of model collapse look like?}
At what contamination level does statistical detection become possible, how does this boundary depend on observation length and statistical method, and what structure does the landscape exhibit?
Iterative training produces short, noisy time series (often fewer than 15 points per generation sequence), where detection power drops sharply~\cite{boettiger2012limits}, and existing analyses leave these dependencies unresolved.
Our detection mechanism (Granger-causal temporal precedence) differs from critical-slowing-down indicators, as model collapse is a first-order transition~\cite{truong2026phase} (\S\ref{sec:related_work}).

We systematically map this landscape using Pythia-410M~\cite{biderman2023pythia} across thirteen contamination levels with multi-seed replication, applying five statistical methods from econometrics~\cite{granger1974spurious,toda1995statistical} to identical data.
The resulting map reveals structured terrain: blind zones where collapse proceeds undetected, a sharp onset where detection jumps from null to reliable within a 5-percentage-point boundary, a synchronous dip where canary and downstream metrics collapse simultaneously, and a detection boundary $\alpha_c(T)$ that follows a power law in observation length.
Cross-architecture validation across five families (345M--6.9B) confirms the landscape generalizes when entropy-diversity coupling is preserved.
Granger precedence establishes temporal predictive improvement, not true causality~\cite{shojaie2022granger}; our canary claim is scoped to diversity metrics (distinct-$n$~\cite{li2016diversity}).

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Detectability landscape characterization} (\S\ref{sec:regime}--\ref{sec:intervention}).
    PermG reveals a detection boundary $\alpha_c(T) = 0.193 + 75.68 \cdot T^{-2.41}$ ($R^2{=}0.883$) with step-like onset ($k{=}100$); predict-then-verify at $T{=}20$ achieves 3/5 exact matches (4/5 under FDR correction; Appendix~\ref{app:t20_prediction_timeline}).
    Canary-triggered cessation reduces peak perplexity by 58\% (proof-of-concept).

    \item \textbf{Formal motivation for canary metric selection} (\S\ref{sec:cascade}).
    Under mode amplification, entropy Granger-precedes diversity (Proposition~\ref{thm:entropy_leads}), with a ${\geq}1$-generation lag (Proposition~\ref{prop:div_lag}), confirmed in 15/15 experiments ($\alpha \geq 0.30$).

    \item \textbf{Method sensitivity as a primary finding} (\S\ref{sec:mmct}--\ref{sec:dose_response}).
    Five detection methods yield null-control FPR from 0\% to 92\%; the same Granger test shifts from 0/8 to 6/8 across a 5-percentage-point boundary.
    The detectability landscape one observes depends critically on the statistical method used to probe it.
\end{enumerate}
